content.title: About
content.content: A beef and cheese taco is a classic Mexican dish consisting of a corn tortilla filled with seasoned ground beef, melted cheese, and often topped with onions, cilantro, and salsa. The corn tortilla gives a distinct flavor and a slightly crunchy texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn tortillas have been used in Mexico for over 3,000 years.
The word “taco” entered English usage in the early 20th century.
Traditional taco beef is marinated in lime juice and spices such as cumin and chili powder.
In the United States more than 4 billion tacos are consumed each year.
While cheddar is common in the U.S., Mexican tacos often use queso fresco or cotija.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Beef provides a complete source of protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in iron
items.content: Beef supplies easily absorbed heme iron, supporting healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Corn tortilla offers fiber
items.content: Corn flour contains dietary fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and cheese are good sources of B12, B6, and niacin, which support the nervous system.

items.title: High saturated fat
items.content: Large amounts of cheese and fatty beef can raise cholesterol if eaten frequently.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Seasonings and cheese often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy allergy.

items.title: Pathogen contamination
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor Salmonella or E. coli.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve tacos hot, folding the tortilla in half. Top with fresh cilantro, lime wedges, salsa, guacamole, or sour cream. For a lighter version, use lean beef and low‑fat cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared tacos in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Keep dry tortillas in a sealed bag at room temperature. Beef can be frozen for up to 3 months, and cheese for up to 2 months.
